citations.title: License fees and annual renewal
citations.requirement: License is not issued until the fee is paid. Licenses expire at the end of the calendar year. Initial license runs up to 15 months. Renew annually.

citations.title: LME/MCO letter of support for residential facility licensure
citations.requirement: Residential applicants (except ICF/IID) must submit an LME/MCO letter of support with the DHSR application.

citations.title: Operating a licensable facility without a license
citations.requirement: Operating a licensable facility without a license is a Class H felony with a $1,000 per day fine. Admit no second adult before the license is issued.

citations.title: Scope (Subchapter 27G)
citations.requirement: Core rules (.0100-.0900) apply to all facilities. Service rules (.5600) modify or expand them. Contract services must follow the rules. Noncompliance is grounds for DHSR to deny or revoke the license.

citations.title: General definitions
citations.requirement: Defines incident (.0103(b)(32)), client (includes legally responsible person for consent), governing body (owner if no board), documentation (dated, authenticated), residential service and staff member.

citations.title: Staff definitions
citations.requirement: Direct Support Professional needs a GED or diploma and a supervision plan made at hire and reviewed annually. Defines QP, AP and paraprofessional. Non-QPs are supervised by a QP with the population served.

citations.title: Governing body policies
citations.requirement: Written policies are required on 18 listed topics: admission/discharge criteria, record management, QA/QI plan and committee, fatality review, medication, incident reporting, fees, medical emergencies, transportation, training, safety and grievances. Keep governing body minutes permanently.

citations.title: Personnel requirements
citations.requirement: Job descriptions signed by staff and supervisor. Staff must be 18+, with no substantiated HCPR findings. Applicants disclose convictions. Training covers orientation, rights/confidentiality, plan needs and bloodborne pathogens. One first-aid/CPR/Heimlich-trained staff on site. Infection-control policy (.0202(i)).

citations.title: Competencies of qualified professionals and associate professionals
citations.requirement: QPs/APs must show knowledge and skills required by the population served. APs get an individualized supervision plan at hire and are supervised by a QP for the period set in .0104. (Text from APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Competencies and supervision of paraprofessionals
citations.requirement: Paraprofessionals are supervised by an AP or QP and must show knowledge and skills for the population. A policy must start an individualized supervision plan at hire. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Assessment and treatment/habilitation or service plan
citations.requirement: Assessment before services. Plan within 30 days of admission, made with the client or legally responsible person. Plan has outcomes with dates, strategies, responsible staff, review at least annually and written consent. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Client records
citations.requirement: Record has face sheet, diagnosis, screening/assessment, plan, emergency contacts, signed emergency-care consent, service notes, progress notes, orders, labs and medication error documentation. AIDS information disclosed only per G.S. 130A-143. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Emergency plans and supplies
citations.requirement: Written fire plan and disaster plan approved by local authority. Evacuation routes posted. Fire and disaster drills at least quarterly in 24-hour facilities, repeated for each shift, simulating fire. First aid supplies accessible. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Client services
citations.requirement: 24-hour services are available every day of the year. Meals must be nutritious. Activities are age-suitable and clients help plan them. Vehicles carrying clients with physical handicaps need secure adaptive equipment. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Medication requirements
citations.requirement: Written orders required. Only licensed persons, or unlicensed staff trained by an RN/pharmacist and privileged, may administer. MAR is recorded immediately. Locked storage at 59-86°F (fridge 36-46°F). Disposal records witnessed. Psychotropic regimen review every 6 months. Report errors immediately to a physician or pharmacist.

citations.title: Compliance with building codes
citations.requirement: Facility must comply with the NC Building Code. It must keep documented evidence of compliance with fire, sanitation and building codes, including an annual fire inspection. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Facility construction/alterations/additions
citations.requirement: Before construction, use change, alterations or additions, consult the DHSR Construction Section and local building and fire officials. Obtain all required local permits. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Location and exterior requirements
citations.requirement: Site needs fire protection, approved water/sewage/waste services and compliance with zoning. Enough outdoor area for clients' right to outdoor activity (G.S. 122C-62). Grounds kept safe and clean, free of insects and rodents. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Facility design and equipment
citations.requirement: Bedrooms: 100 sq ft single, 160 sq ft double, max two per room, same sex. At least one full bath per five persons including staff. Hot water 100-116°F. Fire-retardant mattresses. No unfinished basement or attic sleeping. Cooling not required in 24-hour homes of six or fewer.

citations.title: License required
citations.requirement: No one may establish or operate a licensable facility without first applying for and receiving a DHSR license. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: License issuance
citations.requirement: Apply at least 30 days before planned operation. Disclose owners holding 5% or more. DHSR inspects before issuing. A license is specific to the premises, and each site needs a separate license. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Operations during licensed period
citations.requirement: Post the DHSR complaint hotline number in a public place. Never exceed licensed capacity. Inspections are unannounced, about every 12 months. 30 days' written notice for renovation, capacity, program, location, ownership or name changes and for closure. Renewal needs fee, fire report, sanitation report and ownership list. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: License denial, amendment or revocation
citations.requirement: DHSR may deny a license, or issue provisional status for 30 days to 6 months, which must be posted and disclosed to clients. It revokes for noncompliance that endangers clients and may order summary suspension. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Letter of support required for licensure of residential facilities
citations.requirement: Written request to the LME with capacity, services, location and population. The LME decides on local need for supervised living beds and must respond within five business days. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Client Rights Committee
citations.requirement: The area board oversees client rights. It may require contract agencies to form a Client Rights Committee, which reviews grievances, alleged rights violations and restrictive procedures. Contract agencies report rights incidents to the area director within 30 days and to the board within 90. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Definitions (incident levels; provider categories)
citations.requirement: Level I, II and III incidents are defined. Level III includes death, sexual assault, permanent impairment or a threat to safety. Category A providers are licensed 24-hour residential facilities. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Incident response requirements for Category A and B providers
citations.requirement: Written policy for level I-III incidents with corrective and preventive measures within 45 days. For level III, secure the record and convene an internal review team within 24 hours. Preliminary findings within 5 working days. Owner-signed final report within 3 months.

citations.title: Incident reporting requirements for Category A and B providers
citations.requirement: Report level II (non-death) and level III incidents and level II deaths to the LME within 72 hours on the Secretary's form. Send level III reports to DMH/DD/SAS and level III deaths to DHSR within 72 hours. Submit quarterly summary reports to the LME.

citations.title: Referral of complaints to LMEs (Category A/B providers)
citations.requirement: The LME responds to complaints about licensed providers. It forwards rule-related complaints about Category A providers to DHSR. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Local monitoring
citations.requirement: LME monitors providers using incident history, complaints and QI activities. Accreditation by COA, CQL, CARF or The Joint Commission is a monitoring factor. Corrections are due within 60 days of the monitoring report. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Requirements concerning the need for protective services
citations.requirement: If there is reasonable cause to believe a disabled adult is abused, neglected or exploited, procedures under G.S. 108A Article 6 are initiated. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: LME requirements concerning complaints
citations.requirement: Clients are told in writing of their right to contact the LME, DMH/DD/SAS, DHSR, DSS and Disability Rights North Carolina. LME decides within 5 working days whether to handle informally or investigate. Informal-process letter within 15 working days. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Disclosure of financial interest of providers to potential clients
citations.requirement: Before or at referral to another provider in which the referrer holds a financial interest (owner, employee, family member or affiliate), disclose and document the interest to the potential client. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Supervised living - Scope
citations.requirement: 24-hour home environment. Licensed if it serves 2+ adults or 1+ minor. Minors and adults may not live together. 'C' designation serves adults whose primary diagnosis is a developmental disability.

citations.title: Supervised living - Staff
citations.requirement: At least one staff present whenever any adult client is on the premises, unless the plan documents the client can stay alone. Review that finding at least annually. Staffing above the minimum is set by the facility to meet individual needs.

citations.title: Supervised living - Operations
citations.requirement: Maximum six clients with developmental disabilities. Coordinate with the QPs responsible for habilitation or case management. Support family contact and send annual progress reports to the legally responsible person. Offer choice-based, community-inclusive activities.

citations.title: Requirements for State/County Special Assistance recipients
citations.requirement: Be rule-compliant before admitting Special Assistance recipients or receiving payment. Keep Secretary-required forms signed by a QP in the record, renewed annually. Submit DSS-1464 Civil Rights Compliance Form on request. (Text from APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Death reporting requirements
citations.requirement: Report deaths to DHSR on the G.S. 122C-31 form. Written notice is immediate for death within 7 days of restraint or seclusion, and within 3 days for violence, accident, suicide or homicide. Notify law enforcement for medical-examiner cases and tell next of kin about autopsy. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Summary suspension of public funding authorization
citations.requirement: DMH/DD/SAS may suspend state/federal funding authorization when a client's health, safety or welfare is in immediate jeopardy. A contested case hearing request does not stay the order. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Revocation of authorization to receive public funding
citations.requirement: DMH/DD/SAS revokes funding authorization and may recommend Medicaid disenrollment after written warning for substantial failure to comply. Failure includes altering documents or missing plan-of-correction deadlines. (APSM 30-01, 11/1/11 edition.)

citations.title: Policy on rights restrictions and interventions
citations.requirement: Governing body policy must implement G.S. 122C-59, -65 and -66. If restrictions or restrictive interventions are allowed, name which are permitted, who informs the client, due process, who authorizes and reviews, and the appeal process.

citations.title: Informing clients
citations.requirement: Give each client or legally responsible person a rights summary and tell them of the right to contact the Governor's Advocacy Council. Within 72 hours in a 24-hour facility, explain house rules, confidentiality, grievance, fees, suspension and search policies. Document in the record.

citations.title: Least restrictive alternative
citations.requirement: Use the least restrictive setting and methods. Promote alternatives to injurious behavior, offer meaningful choices, share decision control, and use restrictive interventions only as a last resort by trained staff.

citations.title: Prohibited procedures
citations.requirement: Prohibits corporal punishment (G.S. 122C-59), painful body contact, electric shock, insulin shock, noxious tastes or substances and painful stimuli used to reduce behavior. The governing body may also prohibit others.

citations.title: Seclusion, physical restraint, isolation time-out and protective devices
citations.requirement: Emergency use only for imminent danger, never for convenience or staffing. Staff authorize up to 15 minutes, then a professional must. Orders last 4 hours for adults. Check every 15 minutes and monitor 30 minutes afterward. Document, notify, log and review quarterly.

citations.title: Client's personal funds
citations.requirement: Rule governs client personal funds in 24-hour facilities. Title confirmed from the OAH rule index only. Read the full text before drafting the funds policy.

citations.title: Storage and protection of clothing and possessions
citations.requirement: Rule governs storage and protection of clients' clothing and possessions in 24-hour facilities. Title confirmed from the OAH rule index only. Read the full text before drafting.

citations.title: Living environment
citations.requirement: Rule governs the living environment for clients in 24-hour facilities. Title confirmed from the OAH rule index only. Read the full text before drafting.

citations.title: Health, hygiene and grooming
citations.requirement: Rule governs health, hygiene and grooming supports for clients in 24-hour facilities. Title confirmed from the OAH rule index only. Read the full text before drafting.

citations.title: Additional rights of clients in 24-hour facilities
citations.requirement: Referenced in 27G .0303(b) and 27E .0104(e)(15). Rights restrictions under 122C-62(b)/(d) must be documented per 122C-62(e), and restrictive interventions count as restrictions. Statute text not fetched.

citations.title: Protection of the Abused, Neglected or Exploited Disabled Adult Act
citations.requirement: Cited in 10A NCAC 26C .0303(i) and 27G .0610 as the procedure to start when a disabled adult may be abused, neglected or exploited. Statute text not fetched.

citations.title: Innovations Waiver - Residential Supports
citations.requirement: Approved 1915(c) waiver including Residential Supports. Payment is through the LME/MCO Tailored Plan. Medicaid does not pay room and board. Renewal period reported as July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2029.

citations.cite: NC Medicaid - Innovations Waiver provider accreditation requirement (post of 2026-04-16)
citations.title: National accreditation for Residential Supports providers
citations.requirement: National accreditation is required for enrollments after April 20, 2026. Enrolled providers must re-enroll and report accreditation by April 20, 2027. Confirm accreditor list and service coverage in the NCTracks Provider Permission Matrix.

citations.title: Innovations direct care worker rate increases (SFY 2027)
citations.requirement: Residential Supports DCW add-on of $7.68 per diem. Provider must attest to the LME/MCO and track use of funds for DCW wages. Confirm with the LME/MCO whether it is already in the plan's rate.

citations.title: HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules
citations.requirement: Cited in 10A NCAC 27G .0603(a)(6) for incident confidentiality. Applies to the provider as a Medicaid-billing covered entity. Regulation text not fetched.

citations.title: OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard
citations.requirement: Employee exposure control and training. Complements 10A NCAC 27G .0202(g)(4), which requires bloodborne pathogen training for all staff. Federal text not fetched.

citations.title: HCBS settings requirements
citations.requirement: Home and community-based settings standards (privacy, choice, access, controlled personal space) apply to Innovations residential settings. Federal text not fetched.

policies.title: Governing Body, Chain of Command and Delegation of Management Authority
state_specifics: Governing body is the owner if there is no board (.0103(b)). Name the owner/board, the Program Director and the QP.
Chain of command: governing body, Program Director/QP, shift lead, direct support staff. Name who is in charge when the Program Director is absent.
Keep governing body minutes permanently (.0201).
Non-QP staff are supervised by a QP with experience in the population served (.0104).
The governing body adopts written policies on all 18 topics listed in .0201.

policies.title: Criteria for Discharge, Notice and Recipients
state_specifics: List the discharge reasons: mutual agreement, needs beyond program scope, safety risk, loss of authorization or funding, and the individual's choice.

Written notice goes to the individual, the legally responsible person, the LME/MCO care coordinator and the QP. The notice period is provider-set and no shorter than 60 days where the person may need continuing care (G.S. 122C-63).
An individualized discharge plan is required (G.S. 122C-61).
Non-voluntary discharge follows the suspension and expulsion policy (SUS-01).

policies.title: Client Record Management, Confidentiality and Access
state_specifics: Record contents (.0206): face sheet, diagnosis, assessment, plan, emergency contacts, signed emergency-care consent, service notes, progress notes, orders, labs and medication error documentation.
Safeguard records against loss, tampering and defacement. Keep them in locked storage and secure them when records are moved between sites or transported.
Authorized users have access at all times. Individuals and their legally responsible person may obtain their own information.
AIDS information is disclosed only as G.S. 130A-143 allows (.0206).
Retention period: set it to the longest of the LME/MCO contract and Medicaid requirements. Confirm the number of years before adopting.

policies.title: Safe Transportation of Clients
state_specifics: Transportation guidelines are tailored to each individual's needs, for example seating, wheelchair securement and behavioral supports.
Vehicles carrying clients with physical handicaps need secure adaptive equipment (.0208).
Carry emergency information in every vehicle: contacts, diagnoses, allergies, medications and consent. Staff must be able to reach it in transit.
Verify driver licensing, auto insurance and NC financial responsibility requirements before adopting driver rules.
Record vehicle incidents under the incident policy (GOV-06).

policies.title: QA/QI Committee, Quality Plan and Fatality Review
state_specifics: Written QA/QI plan and committee. Name its members and meeting schedule.
Monitor and evaluate quality of care, outcomes and service utilization. Use incident, complaint and mortality data.
The QP provides professional supervision. The committee reviews staff qualifications and grants habilitation privileges.
Review all fatalities of active clients in residential programs. See HLT-02.
Adopt operational and programmatic performance standards. LME monitoring considers QI activity and accreditation (.0608), and corrections are due within 60 days of a monitoring report.

policies.title: Incident Reporting (Level I, II, III) and IRIS
state_specifics: Level I, II and III definitions (.0602). Level III includes death, sexual assault, permanent impairment or a threat to safety.
Written response policy (.0603): corrective and preventive measures within 45 days. For Level III, secure the record and convene an internal review team within 24 hours.
Level III review: preliminary findings within 5 working days and an owner-signed final report within 3 months.

Report Level II (non-death) and Level III incidents and Level II deaths to the LME within 72 hours on the Secretary's form (.0604). Send Level III reports to DMH/DD/SAS and Level III deaths to DHSR within 72 hours. File quarterly summaries with the LME.
Describe how reports are entered in IRIS, who enters them and how prevention measures are tracked.

policies.title: Client Fee Assessment and Collection
state_specifics: Inform clients or legal representatives of all fees. Explain fees within 72 hours of admission in a 24-hour facility (27D .0201).
Medicaid Innovations Residential Supports does not pay room and board. Charge room and board from the resident's own income.
The 2026 SSI federal benefit rate for an individual is $994 per month. Never charge more than the resident can pay, and verify each person's income.
State/County Special Assistance recipients: follow .5604, including the annual QP-signed forms in the record and DSS-1464 on request.
Document how fees are assessed, collected and receipted.

policies.title: Medical Preparedness Plan and Use in a Medical Emergency
state_specifics: At least one staff member trained in first aid, CPR and the Heimlich maneuver is on site (.0202). CPR must be in person, not online-only.
A signed emergency-care consent is in each record (.0206).
First aid supplies are accessible (.0207).
Procedure: call 911, then notify the guardian, QP, nurse consultant and LME/MCO care coordinator, and complete an incident report if one is required.
Staff send the face sheet, medication list and consent with the person to the hospital.

policies.title: Use of Volunteers
state_specifics: State whether volunteers are used. If not, state that none are used.
If volunteers are used, define their services, orientation, training and supervisor. Volunteers do not count toward staffing minimums.
Volunteers sign a confidentiality agreement and receive rights training.
Volunteers in direct client care are trained in approved de-escalation techniques (27E .0107).
Apply background checks as for staff.

policies.title: Staff Training and Ongoing Education
state_specifics: Training covers orientation, client rights and confidentiality, the needs in each individual's plan, and bloodborne pathogens (.0202).
At least one staff member trained in first aid, CPR and the Heimlich maneuver is on site at all times. CPR must be in person.
Medication administration training must be in person, by an RN, pharmacist or other qualified trainer.
DHSR provides no training. The provider sources trainers and keeps records. Annual hours are not set in the sources, so adopt the hours your accreditor and LME/MCO require.
Direct Support Professionals need a GED or diploma. Supervision follows .0104.

policies.title: Infection Control, Communicable Disease and Bloodborne Pathogens
state_specifics: Written infection control policy (.0202(i)). It covers identifying, reporting, investigating and controlling infectious and communicable diseases in staff and clients.
Bloodborne pathogen training is required for all staff (.0202(g)(4)).
Include an exposure control plan, universal precautions and sharps handling.
Staff with communicable disease follow work-restriction rules. Notify the local health department when required.
Train staff on infectious disease during orientation and annually.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27G .0204 Competencies and Supervision of Paraprofessionals
policies.title: Individualized Supervision Plan for Paraprofessional Staff
state_specifics: Start an individualized supervision plan at hire for every paraprofessional (DSP).
Name who develops it: the QP or associate professional supervisor.
The plan lists the staff member's areas of need and the methods to address them.
Both the staff member and the supervisor review and sign the plan.
Review the plan at least annually (.0104). Paraprofessionals are supervised by an AP or QP.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27G .0205 Assessment and Treatment/Habilitation or Service Plan
policies.title: Referral, Admission and Assessment
state_specifics: Complete an assessment before services. It covers the presenting problem, needs and strengths, a provisional or admitting diagnosis, and an established diagnosis within 30 days.
Also cover social, family and medical history and the evaluations the person's needs call for.
If services start before the plan is in place, document the strategies in use.
Admit adults only ('C' designation, primary diagnosis of a developmental disability), with a maximum of six clients. Admit no second adult before the DHSR license is issued.
Admissions come through the LME/MCO choice list and authorization. Confirm Innovations eligibility and level of support.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27G .0205 Assessment and Treatment/Habilitation or Service Plan
policies.title: Person-Centered Habilitation Plan and Individual Plan
state_specifics: Develop the plan within 30 days of admission, or before if applicable, with the client and/or legally responsible person.
Include outcomes with projected dates, strategies, responsible staff, review at least annually and the basis for evaluating outcomes.
Obtain written consent, or document why consent was not obtained.
Align with the Innovations person-centered plan from the LME/MCO care coordinator.
Send annual progress reports to the legally responsible person (.5603).

policies.title: Fire Safety Plan, Disaster Plan, Drills and Emergency Supplies
state_specifics: Written fire safety plan for each facility and a disaster plan approved by the local authority. Keep the Emergency Management (OEM) verification for the licensure review.
Plans are accessible to staff. Post evacuation routes and procedures.
Hold fire and disaster drills at least quarterly in a 24-hour facility, repeated for each shift. Drills simulate actual fire emergencies.
Keep basic first aid supplies accessible, and keep documentation of the annual fire inspection (.0301).
Facilities with 4–6 clients, or two-story homes, need two remotely located exits per occupied story.

policies.title: Medication Program Scope, Dispensing, Packaging and Labeling
state_specifics: Item 16 (agency does not handle medications) is not adopted: the home administers and stores medications. State this in the manual.

Staff do not prescribe or dispense and keep no stock of prescription drugs. Dispensing is only by a pharmacist, physician or other person authorized by law, on a written order. The methadone clause does not apply.
Non-prescription containers keep the manufacturer's label and a visible expiration date.
Prescriptions are in tamper-resistant packaging. Labels show client name, prescriber, dispensing date, directions, drug name, strength, quantity, expiration and pharmacy details.
Check labels against orders on receipt, and return mislabeled medication to the pharmacy.

policies.title: Medication Administration and MAR
state_specifics: Administer only on a written order from a legally authorized prescriber.
Self-administration only if the physician authorizes it in writing.
Only licensed persons, or unlicensed staff trained by an RN, pharmacist or other qualified professional and privileged, may administer.
Keep a current MAR for each client and record each dose immediately: client name, drug name, strength, quantity, instructions, date and time, and staff name or initials.
Document client requests for medication changes and file them with the MAR. Then consult the physician.

policies.title: Medication Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Store in a securely locked cabinet in a clean, well-lit, ventilated room at 59–86°F. Refrigerators run at 36–46°F, and medications sit in a separate locked compartment if food is also stored.
Store each client's medication separately, and keep external and internal products separate. Provide secure storage if a physician approves self-medication.
Dispose of medication so as to prevent diversion or accidental ingestion.
Keep a disposal record: client, drug, strength, quantity, date, method and the signatures of the person disposing and a witness.

Non-controlled disposal methods are incineration, flushing into a septic/sewer system, or transfer to a local pharmacy. Dispose of remaining medication promptly, or hold it no more than 30 days after discharge unless the person is expected to return.

policies.title: Medication Review, Errors and Refusals
state_specifics: A physician or pharmacist reviews the drug regimen of clients on psychotropic medication every 6 months.
Record findings and corrective action in the client record.
Report errors and significant adverse drug reactions immediately to the client's physician or pharmacist.
Document medication errors in the record (.0206). Evaluate each error against the incident level definitions.
Document refusals of medication.

policies.title: Search and Seizure
state_specifics: Rule: 10A NCAC 27D .0103. State the conditions for searching a client or living space and for seizing belongings.
State that clients are free from unwarranted invasion of privacy.
Document every search and seizure: scope, reason, procedures followed, description of property seized and its disposition.
Inform clients of the search policy within 72 hours of admission (27D .0201).
Default stance: no routine room searches. Searches happen only for imminent safety risk, under the policy.

policies.title: Periodic Internal Review of Client Rights Compliance
state_specifics: The governing body ensures a compliance review of the Client Rights Rules at least every 3 years.
Keep the 3 most recent written review reports.
Name the reviewer and the corrective-action process.
Include the HCBS settings checks.
If the LME requires a Client Rights Committee, report rights incidents as .0504 requires.

policies.title: Informing Clients of Rights and Facility Policies
state_specifics: Give each client and legally responsible person a written rights summary (G.S. 122C Art. 3). Tell them they may contact Disability Rights NC (the rule text names the Governor's Advocacy Council).

In a 24-hour facility, explain within 72 hours at the person's level of understanding: house rules and penalties, confidentiality (G.S. 122C-52 to -56), how to get a copy of the plan, fees, grievance procedure with contact information and help, suspension and expulsion, and search and seizure.
Give written notice of the right to contact the LME, DMH/DD/SAS, DHSR, DSS and Disability Rights NC (27G .7002).
Explain behavior management systems, possible restrictions, notification after emergency use, and notification of legally responsible persons and of rights restrictions.
Document in the record that rights were fully explained.

policies.title: Informing Staff of Client Rights
state_specifics: Train all staff on client rights at hire and annually.
Each staff member signs an acknowledgment of receipt.
Keep the acknowledgment in the personnel file.
Document the training date and trainer.
Train staff on the rights restriction policy (RRI-01).

policies.title: Social Integration, Community Inclusion and Client Self-Governance
state_specifics: Encourage participation and appropriate interaction among clients and with community non-clients. Do not prohibit interaction unless a written restriction is in the record.
Offer choice-based, community-inclusive activities (.5603). Clients help plan activities (.0208). Support family contact.
Support integrated employment and day choices through the individual plan.
Self-governance: house meetings, a client feedback mechanism, client groups and meeting protocols between clients and staff.
Train staff and clients on self-governance.

policies.title: Informed Consent and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: Inform the person of benefits, risks, alternatives, how long the consent is valid and how to withdraw it.
Obtain written consent per G.S. 122C-57(f) and 27E .0100 for planned interventions. Consent for a planned restrictive intervention may not exceed six months.
Written consent is also required for Antabuse and Depo-Provera when used for non-FDA-approved purposes.
The person's right to consent or refuse is protected (G.S. 122C-57(d)). Refusal is not the sole ground for termination except as the statute states.
Where a legally responsible person consents, still seek the individual's assent and use supported decision-making. Document it all in the record.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27D .0304 Protection From Harm, Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation
policies.title: Protection From Harm, Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation: Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Protect from harm per G.S. 122C-66. Define and prohibit abuse and neglect per 10A NCC 27C .0102.
Document and report ALL alleged or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation to the County DSS (G.S. 108A Art. 6; 27G .0610).
Also report to the Health Care Personnel Registry, the LME/MCO and, as required, law enforcement.
Staff are trained on recognizing, preventing and reporting. Employee misconduct results in repercussions up to dismissal.
Include a policy on sale or purchase of goods or services involving clients, and use-of-force guidelines.

policies.title: Least Restrictive Alternative
state_specifics: Deliver services in the least restrictive and most appropriate settings and methods.
Promote coping and engagement skills and alternatives to injurious behavior.
Offer meaningful choices and share decision-making.
Use restrictive interventions only as a last resort, with dignity and respect, by trained staff.
Review restrictive alternatives at each plan review.

policies.title: Prohibited Procedures
state_specifics: Prohibit corporal punishment (G.S. 122C-59).
Prohibit contingent painful body contact and substances that cause painful bodily reactions (excluding Antabuse).
Prohibit electric shock (excluding medically administered ECT), insulin shock, unpleasant-tasting foodstuffs, and noxious substances such as noise, bad smells or splashing with water.
Prohibit any potentially painful procedure or stimulus used to reduce a behavior (excluding prescribed injections).
The governing body may prohibit additional procedures.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27D .0101 Policy on Rights Restrictions and Interventions
policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Restrictive Interventions: Governing Body Policy
state_specifics: Implements G.S. 122C-59, -65 and -66. Provide to all staff.

Default stance (governing body to confirm): seclusion, isolation time-out, planned physical restraint and behavior-control protective devices are NOT permitted in this home. List other prohibited interventions. If the body elects any, name them and the approved curriculum.
Name the position (Program Director/QP) responsible for informing clients of restrictions and the position that authorizes restrictions.
In a 24-hour facility, staff may not restrict a client's rights except through a documented restriction under G.S. 122C-62(b)/(d), documented under 122C-62(e).
Prescribing safeguards for high-risk medications, especially neuroleptics: prescriber justification, informed consent, periodic review, monitoring for adverse effects and a 6-month review.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27D .0101 Policy on Rights Restrictions and Interventions
policies.title: Due Process, Authorization, Review and Debriefing
state_specifics: Clients who refuse restrictive interventions are afforded due process: notice, a stated reason, a review and an appeal route. Name the appeal process.
Name the position that gives written permission for 24-hour restrictions, and the staff designated to review restrictive intervention use.
Consider the client's physical and psychological well-being before, during and after any intervention. Review health history or assessment at admission for conditions that raise risk.
Debrief with the client, legally responsible person and staff after use. Plan to reduce future use, and document and communicate the outcome.
The Client Rights Committee reviews restrictive procedures where the LME requires it (.0504).

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27E .0103 General Policies Regarding Intervention Procedures
policies.title: Intervention Procedures as Therapeutic Treatment
state_specifics: Interventions are used as treatment only when clinically or medically justified.
Only a physician or licensed practicing psychologist, formally trained and privileged in the procedure, may determine and authorize it.
The home does not offer such interventions by default.
Never use an intervention for staff convenience or as punishment.
Document the justification and authorization in the record.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27E .0104 Seclusion, Physical Restraint, Isolation Time-Out, and Protective Devices Used for Behavioral Control
policies.title: Restrictive Interventions: Scope, Limits and Emergency Use
state_specifics: Applies to all staff involved in client care. If no restrictive interventions are permitted (RRI-01 default), this policy states they are not allowed and staff call 911 in an emergency. The rest applies only if the governing body elects emergency use.
Emergency use is only for imminent danger. Never use for coercion, punishment, retaliation, staff convenience or inadequate staffing, or in a way that causes harm.
Staff may authorize up to 15 minutes, then a qualified professional must authorize. Adult orders last up to 4 hours.
Check every 15 minutes with continuous monitoring and documentation, and monitor for 30 minutes afterward.
Discontinue at any risk indicator or once the client regains control.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27E .0104 Seclusion, Physical Restraint, Isolation Time-Out, and Protective Devices Used for Behavioral Control
policies.title: Seclusion/Restraint: Staff Roles, Rooms, Documentation, Notification, Review and Data
state_specifics: Try positive, less restrictive alternatives first. Define how staff are identified, trained and evaluated for competence, and their roles during an intervention.
Seclusion and isolation rooms must be DHSR-approved. The default is that no such room exists.
Document rationale, methods, debriefing and post-intervention well-being checks in the record.

Notify the habilitation team/designee and a governing body designee within 24 hours. Notify the legally responsible person of a minor or incompetent adult immediately, unless they asked not to be notified.

Keep a log: client, professional, date/time/type, duration, reason, alternatives considered, debriefing and adverse effects. Review quarterly, investigate unusual patterns, analyze data and set procedures for planned interventions.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27E .0105 Protective Devices; .0106 Intervention Advisory Committee
policies.title: Protective Devices and Intervention Advisory Committee
state_specifics: A protective device requires a documented necessity. The employee using it must be trained and competent. Document observation and interventions in the record, and set a maintenance and cleaning protocol.
Where the facility is operated by or under contract with an area program (LME), the Client Rights Committee reviews protective device use in the plan.
An Intervention Advisory Committee is required only if restrictive interventions are used as planned interventions. State that it is not applicable if none are used.
If required: document membership, how client information is disseminated and why, and the committee's training and orientation.
Review committee activity annually.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27E .0107 Training on Alternatives to Restrictive Interventions; .0108 Training in Seclusion, Physical Restraint, and Isolation Time-Out
policies.title: Training in De-escalation and in Restrictive Interventions
state_specifics: All staff, service providers, employees, students and volunteers involved in client care are trained in an approved de-escalation curriculum, with a formal annual refresher.
Keep training records at least 3 years: participants, pass/fail, dates and instructor names. Keep instructor initial and refresher records 3 years.
Document instructor qualifications and training requirements. Name the approved curriculum.

If restraint or seclusion is not used, state that the agency will not use restrictive interventions. If used, only staff trained and current in the approved curriculum may use them, with in-person training and a formal annual refresher.
Restrictive-intervention instructors are retrained at least annually and are currently CPR-trained.

policies.title: Suspension, Expulsion and Involuntary Discharge
state_specifics: Each client is free from threat or fear of unwarranted suspension or expulsion.
State the criteria for suspension, expulsion or other discharge not mutually agreed upon.
Document the time frame for resuming services after a suspension, and the specific conditions and timeline for resuming.
Document staff efforts to identify alternative services that meet the person's needs, and designate those services. Write any needed discharge plan.
Inform clients of this policy within 72 hours of admission, and notify the LME/MCO.

policies.title: Health Care Personnel Registry and Criminal Record Checks
state_specifics: Check all unlicensed staff with possible direct access to clients or their property through the HCPR (G.S. 131E-256).
Complete the HCPR check within 90 days of the licensure review. Do not employ anyone with substantiated HCPR findings (.0202).
Complete a criminal record check within 180 days of the application review for every staff member.
Report allegations to the HCPR and cooperate with investigations. Submit investigation results and document each step.
Keep results in the personnel file.

policies.category: G.S. 122C-63 Continuity of Care for Individuals
policies.title: Continuity of Care: Closure and Discharge Notification
state_specifics: Designate the position (Program Director) that notifies the LME/MCO serving the client's county of residence.
Give notice at least 60 days before closing the facility or discharging a client who may need continuing care.
Also give DHSR 30 days' written notice before closure (.0404).
Coordinate transition planning with the care coordinator, family and guardian.
Document the notice and the transition plan in the record.

policies.category: Treatment Rights in 24-hour Facilities: G.S. 122C-61 and G.S. 122C-62 Additional Rights
policies.title: Treatment Rights and Adult Client Rights in a 24-Hour Facility
state_specifics: Every client receives necessary treatment for physical ailments. Each has the right to an individualized discharge plan, and unanticipated discontinuation of treatment is handled under the plan.
Adult rights under G.S. 122C-62: confidential phone calls and visitors 8:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. (at least 6 hours daily, 2 after 6:00 p.m.). Visits do not take precedence over therapies.
Time outdoors daily, exercise facilities several times a week, personal clothing and possessions, religious worship, a driver's license unless prohibited, and individual private storage space.
State-law visiting hours are a minimum. The HCBS settings rule requires visitors at any time unless modified in the plan.
Minors' rights (G.S. 122C-62): not applicable, because 'C' homes serve adults only (.5601). Minors and adults may not live together.

policies.title: Living Environment, Health, Hygiene and Grooming
state_specifics: Single bedrooms 100 sq ft, double 160 sq ft, no more than two per room, same sex. At least one full bathroom per 5 persons including staff and their family.
Hot water 100–116°F. Fire-retardant mattresses. No sleeping in an unfinished basement or attic.
Promote comfort, privacy and personalization. Provide uninterrupted sleep, and let people personalize their space.
Support personal hygiene and grooming with dignity and privacy, and give access to hygiene products.
Smoking is prohibited inside licensed facilities. Post signage.

policies.title: Personal Funds, Clothing and Possessions
state_specifics: Protect clients' personal clothing and possessions. Help each client develop and keep an inventory, and document and monitor belongings.
Assist clients with managing and investing personal funds. Keep a separate ledger for each client with receipts. Never commingle funds.
Document who manages funds, and require written authorization for any deduction.
Do not charge more than the client can pay. SSI is $994 per month for an individual in 2026.
Read the full text of 10A NCAC 27F .0104 and .0105 before final adoption.

policies.title: Facility Pools and Facility Animals (Conditional)
state_specifics: Pools: the home has no pool. If one is added, DHSR Construction Section must approve it and the policy must set staff supervision and safety measures.
Animals: state whether animals are allowed. If they are, require proof of rabies vaccination for owned dogs, cats and ferrets belonging to clients, visitors and staff.
Document and verify the vaccination proof, and keep records for all pets on the premises.
Address allergies, sanitation and infection control.

policies.category: 10A NCAC 27G .3605 Medication and Mobile Units Only
policies.title: Medication and Mobile Units: Not Applicable Statement
state_specifics: 10A NCAC 27G .3605 applies only to medication and mobile units, so it does not apply to this Supervised Living 'C' home.
State this in the manual with a reason, as the worksheet requires for N/A items.
Review if the service model changes.

policies.title: Policies and Procedures Manual: Control, Review and Licensure Submission
state_specifics: Submit the manual with the MH Licensure Policies and Procedures Worksheet, listed first in the required materials order.
Apply at least 30 days before planned operation, and disclose owners holding 5% or more (.0402). The initial fee is $350 for 6 or fewer beds.
Control versions and review at least annually.
Revise after rule, rate or accreditation changes.
DHSR gives applicants 6 months to complete the program review.

policies.title: Required Staff Training Matrix and Special Populations Curriculum
state_specifics: Required: general orientation, client rights, confidentiality, population-specific (I/DD), de-escalation (all staff), and first aid.
Seclusion/restraint training, in person, only if used. Medication administration training, in person, if the home stores or administers.
CPR cannot be online only.
The special populations curriculum must match the I/DD population served.
Keep the curriculum and sign-in rosters for the licensure review.

policies.title: Licensure, Certification, Accreditation and Provider Agreements
state_specifics: A separate license is required for each premises. Maximum is six clients. Operating without a license is a Class H felony with a $1,000 per day fine (G.S. 122C-28).
Licenses expire Dec 31. The initial license can run up to 15 months, then renew annually (G.S. 122C-23). Renewal needs the fee, fire report, sanitation report and ownership list.
DHSR inspections are unannounced, about every 12 months. Post the DHSR complaint hotline number in a public place. Never exceed licensed capacity.

Give DHSR 30 days' written notice of renovation, capacity, program, location, ownership or name changes and closure. DHSR may issue provisional status for 30 days to 6 months, posted and disclosed to clients.

National accreditation is required for Residential Supports: new enrollments after April 20, 2026, and existing providers by April 20, 2027. Confirm the accreditor in the NCTracks Provider Permission Matrix.

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing, Service Documentation, EVV and DCW Attestation
state_specifics: Contract with each Innovations Tailored Plan LME/MCO. Bill only authorized days at the correct level and code (Alliance schedule: H2016, T2014, T2020, H2016 HI). Confirm codes and rates with your plan.
Medicaid does not pay room and board.
File the DCW attestation with the LME/MCO for the $7.68 per diem add-on, and track use of funds for DCW wages.
Confirm in writing whether EVV applies to Residential Supports, and if so complete HHAeXchange onboarding.
LME monitoring: corrections are due within 60 days of the report (.0608). Altered documents or missed plan-of-correction deadlines can lead to funding revocation (26C .0504).

policies.title: Individual Rights, HCBS Settings Requirements, Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act
state_specifics: HCBS settings: residency agreement, privacy, choice of roommate and daily schedule, and food access.
Modify HCBS rights only through a documented, individualized plan modification. Never restrict rights for staff convenience.
Provide interpreters and accessible formats at no cost, and make reasonable accommodations.
Submit DSS-1464 Civil Rights Compliance Form on request for Special Assistance recipients (.5604).
Tell clients in writing they may contact the LME, DMH/DD/SAS, DHSR, DSS and Disability Rights NC.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Written grievance procedure with contact information and help. Give it to clients on admission.
Clients may complain directly to the LME, DMH/DD/SAS, DHSR, DSS or Disability Rights NC.
The LME decides within 5 working days whether to handle informally or investigate. The informal-process letter is due within 15 working days.

documents.title: Policy & Procedure Worksheet (MH Licensure Policies and Procedures Worksheet), including Submission Guidelines
documents.form_number: No form number printed. Submission Guidelines are marked REV 7-22-25 and the checklist pages are marked REV 3-20-25 / 03-20-25. The Initial Application Packet (DHHS/DHSR/MHL5001) calls it the 'MH Licensure Policies and Procedures Worksheets'.
documents.issuer: NC DHHS, Division of Health Service Regulation, Mental Health Licensure & Certification Section (Licensure & Training team)
documents.how_used: This is the primary source of required_items. It is the DHSR checklist that the Licensure & Training reviewer uses to check the written P&P manual (items 1-93, pages 2-27). The provider enters the manual page number for each item and marks Yes/No. Not every item applies to a Supervised Living 'C' home, so a few are marked conditional below.

documents.title: Required Materials for Licensure Review (List of Required Materials for Initial and Change Licensure Review)
documents.issuer: NC DHHS DHSR Mental Health Licensure & Certification Section
documents.version: Link on the Forms page: listmaterials.pdf?ver=1.2
documents.how_used: This is the submission-order checklist for the program review. It tells the provider to 'Submit documents in the same order as listed.' I took only the policy and plan items from it: the P&P manual and worksheet, the training requirements and curriculum, and the written disaster plan with Emergency Management verification. The staff records, instructor credentials and NCID items are excluded as paperwork.

documents.title: Initial Licensure Application Packet
documents.issuer: NC DHHS DHSR Mental Health Licensure & Certification Section
documents.how_used: Process document only. It says to develop written P&Ps for the service and 'DO NOT SEND Policies and Procedures with this application'; they are reviewed later by the Licensure & Training team. It also lists the rule subchapters the P&Ps must be built from. No required_items come from it, because the rest is application paperwork.

documents.title: The Basics of Mental Health Licensing Process (DHSR slide deck)
documents.issuer: NC DHHS DHSR Mental Health Licensure & Certification Section
documents.how_used: Describes how the program review works: the manual and worksheet are submitted, staff must be hired before licensure, a walk-through is done, and the disaster plan is reviewed by the county Emergency Management office. It lists no policy items of its own.

required_items.text: Procedure defining delegation of management authority for the agency's operation and services (chain of command).
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0201 Governing Body Policies; Worksheet p.2

required_items.text: Procedure for criteria for discharge of the client from the facility/agency: reasons a client might be discharged, and the notice period and recipients of the notice.

Procedure on Client Record Management: transportation of records, safeguarding against loss, tampering and defacement, authorized-user access at all times, confidentiality, and providing access to information for clients.
Procedure with guidelines for safe transportation of clients, tailored to individual needs, including securing and accessing emergency information in transit.

Procedures on the composition and activities of a QA/QI committee. Activities include: monitoring and evaluating quality of care, outcomes and service utilization; a written QA/QI plan; professional/clinical supervision by a qualified professional; strategies for improving care; review of staff qualifications and granting of treatment/habilitation privileges; review of all fatalities of active clients in area-operated or contracted residential programs; and adoption of operational and programmatic performance standards.
Procedures for reporting Level I, II and III incidents, including specific measures to prevent similar incidents and how the agency will implement IRIS (Incident Response Improvement System).

Client Fee Assessment and Collection Procedure: how clients or legal representatives are informed of all fees for assessment, treatment and habilitation, and practices for assessing and collecting fees.
Procedures for the agency's medical preparedness plan and how it will be used in a medical emergency.
Procedures on use of volunteers: whether used, services provided, training, supervisor, and how client confidentiality is ensured.
Policy on training for professional and paraprofessional staff: what training is provided and how ongoing staff education is ensured.
Policy on identifying, reporting, investigating and controlling infectious and communicable diseases affecting staff and clients, including training on infectious diseases and blood-borne pathogens.

Policy on implementing and documenting an individualized supervision plan for all paraprofessional staff upon hire. It must specify who develops the plan, the staff's areas of need and methods to address them, and that the plan is reviewed and signed by both staff member and supervisor.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0204 Competencies and Supervision of Paraprofessionals; Worksheet p.4

required_items.text: Admission and Assessment policy: procedure for an admission assessment before services, including presenting problem, needs and strengths, provisional/admitting diagnosis with an established diagnosis within 30 days, social/family/medical history, evaluations appropriate to needs, and documented strategies when services start before the plan is in place.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0205 Assessment and Treatment/Habilitation or Service Plan; Worksheet pp.4-5

required_items.text: Policy on developing a treatment/habilitation plan within 30 days of admission (or before, if applicable), with the client and/or legally responsible person. It must include anticipated outcomes with projected dates, strategies, responsible staff, an at-least-annual review schedule, the basis for evaluating outcomes, and written consent or a written statement of why consent was not obtained.

Emergency Plans and Supplies policy: a written fire safety plan for each facility and an area-wide disaster plan approved by the appropriate local authority; plans accessible to staff and evacuation procedures/routes posted; fire and disaster drills at least quarterly in 24-hour facilities, repeated for each shift; drills simulating actual fire emergencies; basic first aid supplies available.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0207 Emergency Plans and Supplies; Worksheet pp.5-6

required_items.text: The P&P manual documents that the agency chooses NOT to administer medications, and that it will not prescribe, handle, dispense, administer, transport, dispose of or store medications. Complete only if the home does not handle medications.

Medication Dispensing procedure: dispensing only by a registered pharmacist, physician or other person authorized by law and registered with the NC Board of Pharmacy; only on a written order from a licensed M.D.; no stock of prescription drugs for dispensing except in emergencies without hiring a pharmacist; take-home methadone by R.N.s only (applies only to programs licensed to distribute methadone).
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Dispensing Procedures; Worksheet p.6

required_items.text: Medication Packaging and Labeling procedures: manufacturer's label and visible expiration date on non-prescription containers not dispensed by a pharmacist; tamper-resistant packaging for prescriptions (including samples); prescription labels showing client name, prescriber, dispensing date, directions, drug name/strength/quantity/expiration, and pharmacy or dispensing location details and dispensing practitioner.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Packaging and Labeling Procedures; Worksheet p.7

required_items.text: Medication Administration procedures: administration only on a written order from a legally authorized prescriber; self-administration only if authorized in writing by the physician; administration by licensed personnel or unlicensed staff trained by an R.N., pharmacist or other qualified professional; a current MAR for each client, documented immediately after administration (client name, drug name/strength/quantity, instructions, date and time, name or initials of administering person); client requests for medication changes documented and filed with the MAR, followed by physician consultation.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Administration Procedures; Worksheet pp.7-8

required_items.text: Medication Disposal procedures: disposal to prevent diversion or accidental ingestion; a disposal record (client, drug, strength, quantity, date and method, signature of the person disposing and the witness); methods for non-controlled substances (incineration, flushing into septic/sewer, or transfer to a local pharmacy); remaining medication disposed of promptly or held no more than 30 days after discharge unless the client is expected to return.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Disposal Procedures; Worksheet p.8

required_items.text: Medication Storage procedures: a securely locked cabinet in a clean, well-lit, ventilated room at 59-86 degrees F; refrigerator at 36-46 degrees F, with medications in a separate locked compartment if food is also stored; separate storage for each client and for external vs. internal use; secure storage if a physician approves self-medication.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Storage Procedures; Worksheet pp.8-9

required_items.text: Medication Review procedure: 6-month drug review by a physician or pharmacist for clients on psychotropic medications; findings and any corrective action recorded in the client record.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Review Procedures; Worksheet p.9

required_items.text: Medication Error procedures: how errors and significant adverse drug reactions are reported immediately to the client's physician or pharmacist, and how a client's refusal of medication is documented.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27G .0209, Medication Errors Procedures; Worksheet p.9

required_items.text: Search and Seizure policy: conditions for searching a client or living space, including procedures for seizing belongings or property in the client's possession.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0103 Search and Seizure Policy; Worksheet p.9

required_items.text: The search and seizure policy documents that clients will be free from unwarranted invasion of privacy.

The policy states every search and seizure is documented, including scope of search, reason, procedures followed, description of any property seized, and an account of the disposition of seized property.
Policy on how the governing body ensures a compliance review of Client Rights Rules implementation at least every 3 years, with the 3 most recent written review reports kept.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0104 Periodic Internal Review; Worksheet p.10

required_items.text: Informing Clients policy: written summary of rights (G.S. 122C Art. 3) to client and legally responsible person; right to contact Disability Rights NC; timely notification (24-hour facilities within 72 hours, explained at the client's level of understanding); information to be provided (rules and penalties, confidentiality protections G.S. 122C-52 through 56, how to get a copy of the treatment/habilitation plan, and governing body policies on fee assessment/collection, grievance procedures with contact info and assistance, suspension and expulsion, and search and seizure); special considerations for restrictive interventions and restricted rights (behavior management systems, potential restrictions, notification after emergency use, notification of legally responsible persons, notification of rights restrictions); documentation in the client record that rights were fully explained.

Informing Staff policy: how staff are informed about Client Rights and how documentation is maintained, plus a procedure requiring each staff member to sign an acknowledgment of receipt, kept on file.

Social Integration policy (day/night or 24-hour facilities): guidelines for encouraging and facilitating appropriate social interaction among clients and with community non-clients. It covers encouragement of participation, no prohibition of social interaction unless a written restriction is in the client record, and what counts as appropriate interactions.

Client Self-Governance policy (day/night or 24-hour facilities): client input in facility governance with mechanisms for feedback; development of client self-governance groups; meeting and communication protocols between clients and staff; training and support for clients and staff.

Informed Consent policy: informing clients about benefits, risks, alternatives, length of consent validity and withdrawal procedures (consent for planned restrictive intervention not to exceed six months); written consent per G.S. 122C-57(f) or Subchapter 27E .0100 planned interventions, and for drugs such as Antabuse and Depo-Provera when used for non-FDA-approved uses; right to consent or refuse under G.S. 122C-57(d), with refusal not used as the sole ground for termination except as stated; documentation of informed consent in the client record.

Protection From Harm, Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation policy: protection from harm per G.S. 122C-66; definitions and prohibition of abuse and neglect per 10A NCAC 27C .0102; transaction policies on sale or purchase of goods or services involving clients; use of force guidelines; employee conduct repercussions including dismissal; staff training on recognizing, preventing and reporting; documentation and reporting procedures.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0304 Protection From Harm, Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation; Worksheet p.14

required_items.text: Least Restrictive Alternative policy: services delivered in the least restrictive and most appropriate settings and methods; promotion of coping and engagement skills; meaningful activity choices; shared decision-making; restrictive interventions only as a last resort, with dignity and respect, by trained personnel.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0101 Least Restrictive Alternative; Worksheet p.15

required_items.text: Prohibited Procedures policy: clear prohibition of banned interventions, including corporal punishment (G.S. 122C-59), contingent painful body contact, substances that induce painful bodily reactions (excluding Antabuse), electric shock (excluding medically administered ECT), insulin shock, unpleasant-tasting foodstuffs, contingent noxious substances (noise, bad smells, splashing with water), and any potentially physically painful procedure or stimulus used to reduce a behavior (excluding prescribed injections).
Policy with clear guidelines and procedures for restricting client rights and implementing interventions that ensure safety, dignity and respect; provided to all staff.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0101 Policy on Rights Restrictions and Interventions; Worksheet p.16 (numbered '35a' in the document)

required_items.text: Procedures on how ALL instances of alleged or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of clients are documented and reported to the County Department of Social Services.
Procedures and safeguards for prescribing medications that present a serious risk to the client, with special focus on neuroleptic medications.
Identify in the policy any restrictive interventions prohibited from use within the facility.
If the facility operates 24 hours, outline the circumstances and procedures prohibiting staff from restricting a client's rights.
Policy outlining the permitted restrictive interventions and the approved training curriculum; if none are permitted, the policy must explicitly say they are not allowed.
Policy identifies the staff member (position) responsible for informing the client of any restrictions that may be used.
Policy documents that clients who refuse restrictive interventions are afforded due process. (Worksheet pp.16-22: the highlighted items apply if the agency uses restrictive interventions.)
Policy includes the staff position responsible for giving written permission for 24-hour restrictive interventions. (Highlighted; applies if restrictive interventions are used.)
Policy designates the specific staff responsible for review of the use of restrictive interventions. (Highlighted; applies if restrictive interventions are used.)

Policy states what considerations are given to the client's physical and psychological well-being before, during and after a restrictive intervention, including review of health history or a health assessment at admission for pre-existing conditions or limitations that raise risk. (Highlighted; applies if restrictive interventions are used.)

Policy guidelines for debriefing and planning sessions with clients and legally responsible persons to reduce future use: debriefing process, planning process, and documentation/communication to the client and LRP after use. (Highlighted; applies if restrictive interventions are used.)

Policy with guidelines for intervention procedures as therapeutic treatment methods that are clinically or medically justified and authorized by qualified professionals (determination and authorization only by a physician or licensed practicing psychologist formally trained and privileged in the procedure). (Highlighted.)
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0103 General Policies Regarding Intervention Procedures; Worksheet pp.17-18

required_items.text: Policy states that it applies to all staff involved in client care and in implementing restrictive interventions. (Highlighted.)
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0104 Seclusion, Physical Restraint, Isolation Time-Out, and Protective Devices Used for Behavioral Control; Worksheet p.18

required_items.text: Guidelines for the use of seclusion, physical restraint, isolation and protective devices for behavioral management. (Highlighted.)
Procedures outlining limitations on the use of restrictive interventions. (Highlighted.)
Guidelines on prohibited uses, such as coercion, punishment, retaliation, staff convenience or inadequate staffing; interventions must not cause harm or abuse.
Documentation outlining the acceptable use of restrictive interventions within the facility.

Elements for procedures on use of seclusion: positive, less restrictive alternatives tried first; how staff are identified, trained and evaluated for competence; staff responsibilities and professional roles during interventions; documentation and notification protocols after any restrictive intervention; and (continued on p.19) procedures for well-being checks and assessing consequences after the intervention. (Highlighted.)
Guidelines on room requirements for Seclusion and Isolation, if used (DHSR must approve the room).
Guidelines for documenting use of restrictive interventions in client records, including rationale, methods and debriefing. (Highlighted.)
Guidelines for emergency use of restrictive interventions, including time limits and authorization procedures. (Highlighted.)
Guidelines on precautions and actions during restrictive interventions, including continuous monitoring and documentation. (Highlighted.)
Procedures for discontinuing restrictive interventions at any indication of risk to health or safety or once the client gains behavioral control. (Highlighted.)

Notification within 24 hours of the treatment/habilitation team or designee after each use, a governing body designee, and immediate notification of the legally responsible person of a minor or incompetent adult unless they asked not to be notified. (Highlighted.)

Review and Reporting procedures: review time frame set by a governing body designee and the Client Rights Committee, with confidentiality; investigation of unusual or possibly unwarranted patterns of use; a log of client name, responsible professional, date/time/type, duration and reason, alternatives considered and why not used, debriefing and planning with client/LRP/staff, and adverse effects. (Highlighted.)
The agency's data collection and analysis procedures on the use of seclusion and physical restraint. (Highlighted.)
The agency's procedures if planned intervention is used. (Highlighted.)

Protective Devices procedure: necessity for the device; employee using it is trained and competent; observation and interventions documented in the client record; protocol for maintenance and cleaning.

Procedure documenting that, if the facility is operated by or under contract with an area program, use of protective devices in the treatment/habilitation plan is subject to Client Rights Committee review.
An Intervention Advisory Committee shall be established for additional safeguards in a facility that uses restrictive interventions as planned interventions. (Highlighted.)
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0106 Intervention Advisory Committee; Worksheet p.20

required_items.text: Document who is required to join the agency's Intervention Advisory Committee. (Highlighted.)
Procedure governing the Intervention Advisory Committee, detailing how client information is disseminated and the reasoning for it. (Highlighted.)
Procedure documenting the specific training and orientation given to the Intervention Advisory Committee. (Highlighted.)

Policy documents that all staff, service providers, employees, students and volunteers involved in client care must be trained in approved de-escalation techniques as alternatives to restrictive interventions.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0107 Training on Alternatives to Restrictive Interventions; Worksheet p.21

required_items.text: Policy documents a formal annual refresher in an approved de-escalation curriculum for all staff.
Procedures for keeping documentation of alternatives-to-restrictive-intervention training for all staff for at least three years (participants, pass/fail outcomes, training dates, instructor names).
Policy documents the instructor's qualifications and training requirements.
Procedures for maintaining documentation of alternatives training and of initial and refresher instructor training for at least three years.
Policy states that any staff using restrictive interventions must be trained and current in an approved restrictive-intervention training program. (Highlighted.)
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27E .0108 Training in Seclusion, Physical Restraint, and Isolation Time-Out; Worksheet p.22

required_items.text: Documentation of the approved curriculum for restrictive interventions used; if none are used, a policy stating the agency will not use restrictive interventions. (Highlighted.)
Show where in the policy the prerequisite training requirements for staff to use restrictive interventions are outlined. (Highlighted.)
Policy documents a formal annual refresher in an approved restrictive intervention, successfully completed by all staff. (Highlighted.)
Policy states that restrictive-intervention instructors must be retrained at least annually and be currently CPR-trained. (Highlighted.)
Procedures for maintaining initial and refresher instructor training documentation for at least three years. (Highlighted.)
Suspension and Expulsion policy states each client shall be free from threat or fear of unwarranted suspension or expulsion from the facility.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27D .0102 Suspension and Expulsion Policy; Worksheet p.22

required_items.text: Policy outlines criteria for suspension, expulsion or other forms of discharge that are not mutually agreed upon.

Policy sets documentation requirements: time frame for resuming services after a suspension; specific conditions and timeline for resuming services; staff efforts to identify alternative services meeting the client's needs, and designation of those services; any necessary discharge plan.

Health Care Personnel Registry policy: the agency's responsibility to vet all unlicensed staff with possible direct access to clients or their property through the HCPR, and how it will handle report-allegation procedures, investigation procedures, submission of investigation results, and documentation requirements.
required_items.cite: G.S. 131E-256 Health Care Personnel Registry (HCPR); Worksheet p.23

required_items.text: Policy on which staff position of a facility for individuals with intellectual disabilities will notify the LME/MCO serving the client's county of residence of the intent to close the facility or discharge a client who may need continuing care, at least 60 days before the closure or discharge.
required_items.cite: N.C.G.S. 122C-63 Continuity of Care; Worksheet p.23 (the document numbers this '84')

required_items.text: Policy documenting that every client in a 24-hour facility receives necessary treatment for physical ailments, with guidelines on the right to necessary treatment, the right to an individualized discharge plan, and unanticipated discontinuation of treatment.
required_items.cite: N.C.G.S. 122C-61 Treatment Rights in 24-hour Facilities; Worksheet p.24 (the document also numbers this '84', so the id here is disambiguated)

required_items.text: Policy outlining adult clients' rights: confidential phone calls; visitors 8:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. for at least 6 hours daily, 2 after 6:00 p.m., not taking precedence over therapies; communicating and meeting under appropriate supervision with individuals of their choice; visits outside the facility unless commitment or court-order issues; time outdoors daily and access to exercise facilities several times a week; keeping and using personal clothing and possessions; religious worship; retaining a driver's license unless prohibited; individual private storage space.
required_items.cite: N.C.G.S. 122C-62 Additional Rights in 24-hour Facilities; Worksheet p.24

required_items.text: Policy outlining minor clients' rights under G.S. 122C-62 (phone calls, supervised visitors, mail, special education and vocational training, outdoor play and recreation, personal clothing and possessions, religious worship, storage space, spending a reasonable sum of their money, driver's license). Likely not applicable to a 'C' (adult) home, but the worksheet's 'No/N/A' rule requires a comment explaining why.

Living Environment policy: how the agency provides each client a living environment that promotes comfort, privacy and personalization, with guidelines ensuring uninterrupted sleep, personal privacy and the ability to personalize living space.

Health, Hygiene and Grooming policy: guidelines for personal health, hygiene and grooming care that respect client rights and dignity, including the right to dignity, privacy and humane care, opportunities for personal hygiene, access to hygiene products, and facilities that ensure privacy.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27F .0103 Health, Hygiene and Grooming; Worksheet pp.25-26

required_items.text: Guidelines and procedures for staff to safeguard clients' personal clothing and possessions: efforts to protect belongings, how employees help clients develop and keep an inventory, and procedures for documenting and monitoring personal belongings.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27F .0104 Storage and Protection of Clothing and Possessions; Worksheet p.26

required_items.text: Client's Personal Funds policy: guidelines for assisting clients with managing and investing personal funds, including assistance with personal fund accounts, management of funds by facility employees, and authorization for deductions.
required_items.cite: 10A NCAC 27F .0105 Client's Personal Funds; Worksheet p.26

required_items.text: Facilities With Pools: policy states any agency pool must be approved by the DHSR Construction Section and includes guidelines on staff supervision and safety measures. Conditional; complete only if there is a pool.

official.notes:
SOURCES AND LIMITS. DHSR's Policy & Procedure Worksheet is the single official checklist for the policy content. It is a general mental-health worksheet that cites 10A NCAC 27G .0200, 27D, 27E, 27F and the statutes. It has no items drawn from the Supervised Living rules (10A NCAC 27G .5601-.5604). I could not retrieve the .5600 rule text itself, so no .5600-specific policy items are listed. Item text above is condensed from the form because of quoting limits; the item numbering and rule cites follow the form, and the PDF has the exact wording. The form numbers two different items '84' (G.S. 122C-63 on p.23 and G.S. 122C-61 on p.24); I disambiguated them with bracketed cites. It also has an item '35a'.

HOW IT IS SUBMITTED. Per the Application Packet, do NOT send the P&Ps with the license application. After the zoning, LME/MCO letter of support, floor plan and photo items are in and DHSR Construction has done the physical plant review, the Licensure & Training team contacts the applicant to begin the program review. The applicant has six months from that first contact to finish it; DHSR describes the manual as the licensee's own and says it is returned for revision if incomplete or incorrect.

WORKSHEET RULES (Submission Guidelines, REV 7-22-25):
- Submit the P&P manual as ONE PDF and the worksheet as a SEPARATE PDF.
- List the exact manual page number for each required policy.
- If you answer 'No' or 'N/A', explain why in the comment box.
- Worksheets must be complete and correct; incomplete or incorrect ones are returned.
- Flowcharts are not accepted as policy documents.
- If the agency uses restrictive interventions, complete the highlighted areas on worksheet pages 16-22. I marked those items '(Highlighted)', but the highlighting is hard to read in the PDF text, so confirm against the PDF.
- The slide deck says the worksheet is a guide, not a substitute for the regulations. The Application Packet says to build the P&Ps from 10A NCAC Ch. 26 Subch. C and Ch. 27 Subchs. C, D, E, F and G.

SUBMISSION ORDER. The Required Materials list says to submit documents in the order listed: P&P manual and worksheet; personnel records; staff training; training curriculum; instructor credentials; disaster plan. The 'Substance Abuse Waiver Training' group applies to SUD services only. A written disaster plan with verification from local Emergency Management is required; the county Emergency Management office confirms in writing that the plan was reviewed.

APPLICABILITY TO A SUPERVISED LIVING 'C' HOME (adult DD, 24-hour residential):
- Item 86 (minors' rights) is likely N/A because the population is adults.
- Item 93 (medication and mobile units) is N/A.
- Items 91 (pools) and 92 (animals) apply only if the home has a pool or allows animals.
- Medication items 17-23 apply if the home handles medications; item 16 is the opt-out statement used only if it does not.
- The restrictive-intervention items (35a-79) apply as written if restrictive interventions are used. If none are used, items 40 and 75 require an explicit statement that they are not allowed.
- Item 84 [G.S. 122C-63] is written for facilities serving individuals with intellectual disabilities, so it applies to a 'C' home.

SEPARATE FROM POLICY CONTENT. Staff records, resumes, license verifications, HCPR and criminal checks, instructor credentials, NCID username, application forms, ownership information, fees, floor plan and photos, zoning letter, LME/MCO letter of support, and the fire and sanitation inspections are paperwork, not policy content. The walk-through checklist is a separate pre-licensure inspection. The slide deck says all staff must be hired and in place before a license is granted.
